ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Barbara Jordan

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Jordan is a 44-year-old professor with active primary progressive multiple sclerosis who comes for her yearly preventive visit seven weeks after her four-month review. She had her two ocrelizumab half-doses three months ago and has had no infections since. Her walking is unchanged: she uses her cane on campus and a rollator at home for longer distances. The summer heat makes her legs heavier by the afternoon; her cooling vest and moving her seminars to the morning have helped. She has had no falls; on one hot afternoon in July her legs gave way briefly at home and her rollator caught her. Her bladder is better on mirabegron. She is preparing for the autumn term and several speaking engagements, and her university has put the accommodations she asked for in place. She had her bone density scan this morning. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She wants full treatment for any illness that could be reversed, wants to be told plainly what is happening, and wants to make her own decisions. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and asked that information about her health be shared only with the people she names. She chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
